Scenario: How to use this guide
Actions / suggested test: Ask the test coordinator for the correct portal link and your own test account. Confirm whether payments use the bank’s UAT environment before making a test payment. | Find the chapter for your role. Each procedure gives the menu/page, numbered actions, the expected result, and a suggested test. | Use a unique company CR and tender reference for each test run. Keep the same reference when handing work to the next role. | Record results in the supplied TEST_CHECKLIST.csv. Report a failure with the page, reference, time, exact message and a screenshot.
Expected result: The team can follow one complete vendor-to-tender test and identify the step where a problem occurs.

Scenario: Who does what
Actions / suggested test: Prepare separate accounts for the administrator, procurement user, procurement manager, department requester, department manager, finance reviewer, technical evaluator and commercial evaluator. | Prepare three different committee users: Chairman, Secretary and Member. Assign them to the tender; one shared account cannot replace all three confirmations. | Prepare at least two vendor companies: one successful bidder and one unsuccessful bidder. Add a third invited vendor who does not bid to check recipient boundaries. | Give each person the relevant role permission and company/department assignment. Menu visibility follows those permissions and assignments.
Expected result: Every handover goes to the correct person and company.

Scenario: Sign in, OTP and choose a CR
Actions / suggested test: Try email and CR login; test a shared email with two CRs; confirm another vendor’s CR cannot be opened.
Expected result: The correct staff workspace or vendor CR opens only after the required authentication.

Scenario: Switch between your vendor companies
Actions / suggested test: Invite one CR to a closed tender; switch to another CR and confirm that invitation does not transfer.
Expected result: All actions apply to the selected CR.

Scenario: Create staff users and assign tender responsibilities
Actions / suggested test: Create a technical user in the correct company; confirm selection is available. Check a user assigned to a different company is excluded.
Expected result: Assigned active users are available in tender team selectors and their own inboxes.

Scenario: Set vendor groups and registration fees
Actions / suggested test: Check one paid group and one zero-fee group. Confirm the zero-fee applicant is pending review, not automatically registered.
Expected result: Applicants see the fee and document rules for the selected group.

Scenario: Maintain effective vendor fee records
Actions / suggested test: Open the fee list and choose Add or edit the relevant group’s fee record. | Select the vendor group and Fee Type: Registration Fee or Renewal Fee. Enter the amount/currency and Active From / Active To dates shown by the form. | Make the fee record active for the intended period, then save. | Select that group in a sample registration and confirm the application’s displayed quote before payment.
Expected result: Registration/renewal uses the applicable configured fee record and displays the payable amount.

Scenario: Set group-specific registration documents
Actions / suggested test: Configure two required types for one group. Try submitting with one missing, then upload both. Check a different group gets its own types.
Expected result: Required uploads follow the selected group and cannot be relabelled by the applicant.

Scenario: Maintain grades, categories and specialties
Actions / suggested test: Add/edit grade names, codes, ordering and active status in Vendor Grades. | Maintain categories and subcategories used to describe supplier capabilities. Link each subcategory to its correct category. | Review vendors’ submitted specialties before using them to target closed tenders. | Use the Specialties Filter page to search vendors by their category/subcategory and related filters.
Expected result: Procurement can use clear, maintained grades and specialty filters when selecting vendors.

Scenario: Open the registration page and enter company details
Actions / suggested test: Try a duplicate active CR and a new CR. Confirm the application rejects the duplicate with a clear message.
Expected result: The application identifies the company, its CR and the registration rules to apply.

Scenario: Enter the company location
Actions / suggested test: Change country after selecting a region/city and confirm the form refreshes its dependent choices.
Expected result: The saved location belongs to the selected country and region.

Scenario: Create or reuse the applicant’s login
Actions / suggested test: Enter the applicant’s name and personal login email in Account access. | Enter the applicant’s mobile number accurately, including the required country code. This is the person’s authentication destination when SMS OTP applies. | For a new login, create a password and confirm it. For an existing email, enter its current password to link another CR to that identity. | Check the applicant details before submitting; this person becomes the owner/contact for the new vendor CR.
Expected result: The applicant has one verified login identity with a membership for this CR.

Scenario: Upload the required registration documents
Actions / suggested test: Omit one required document and check submission is refused. Upload it and confirm the registration can continue.
Expected result: Required documents are saved against their correct types on the vendor’s Documents tab.

Role: Applicant in a paid group / waiver applicant asked to pay
Scenario: Pay a registration fee
Actions / suggested test: Run an approved successful payment and an approved cancellation. Check cancellation does not activate the vendor and repeated return does not duplicate the payment.
Expected result: A verified successful payment activates registration for the correct CR; its transaction is recorded for accounting.

Role: Applicant in a waived vendor group
Scenario: Wait for a waiver decision
Actions / suggested test: Confirm pending applicants can see status but cannot use full vendor features. Approve the waiver and confirm access becomes available.
Expected result: Profile, contacts and tenders stay restricted while waiver approval/payment is pending.

Scenario: Review Riyadha and approve a waiver or require payment
Actions / suggested test: Test the approval path and, using another applicant, the custom-payment path. Check zero/negative custom payment amounts cannot be accepted.
Expected result: The reviewer controls waiver approval or a specific payment requirement, with a saved reason.

Scenario: Read the Vendor Workspace and profile checklist
Actions / suggested test: Confirm the company name and CR at the top. Check registration start/expiry and current status. | Review the Profile Checklist: Company profile, Primary contacts, Bank account, Specialties and Required documents. | Use the tabs to complete each outstanding item and return to Overview. | Review Document Expiry and replace documents that have expired or are approaching expiry.
Expected result: The checklist explains what remains before procurement profile review.

Scenario: Add contacts and grant CR-specific portal access
Actions / suggested test: Create Viewer, Bidder and Editor contacts. Confirm the viewer cannot edit or bid, and a linked multi-CR contact gets the CR selector.
Expected result: The contact is linked to this CR with the selected access, without overwriting an existing shared identity.

Scenario: Edit or remove a contact and manage passwords
Actions / suggested test: Edit a phone/designation without re-entering a password. Remove one CR membership from a shared login and check its other valid CR remains accessible.
Expected result: Contact details and CR access stay current; unrelated linked companies retain their own memberships.

Scenario: Add or update a bank account
Actions / suggested test: Enter the bank name, branch, account number, SWIFT and IBAN as applicable. | Upload the bank letterhead/supporting document requested by the form. | Review the details and save. Check the row’s review status. | If rejected/returned, read the reviewer’s reason, correct the information and resubmit through the available edit action.
Expected result: The bank details and supporting file are recorded and routed for review.

Scenario: Maintain company branches
Actions / suggested test: Add the branch name and its contact/location details. | Select country, then its region and city. Enter the branch address. | Save and review the branch’s status. Use Edit for corrections and the removal action when appropriate.
Expected result: Each branch is stored under the selected vendor CR.

Scenario: Maintain credentials
Actions / suggested test: Enter the credential details requested in the form, such as name/reference and relevant dates. | Add any supporting information required by the displayed fields. | Save, check its review status, and use Edit to correct it if the reviewer requests changes.
Expected result: The company’s qualifications/credentials are available for review.

Scenario: Maintain specialties
Actions / suggested test: Check that a subcategory belongs to its selected category and a vendor with a different specialty is not included by that filter.
Expected result: Procurement can identify the company’s capabilities accurately.

Scenario: Upload, preview and replace vendor documents
Actions / suggested test: Open a new PDF and an image after uploading; confirm one vendor cannot open another vendor’s private document.
Expected result: Documents remain attached to the correct vendor and type and can be reviewed by authorised users.

Role: Vendor owner / editor with appropriate access
Scenario: Submit a completed profile or a renewal
Actions / suggested test: Complete every checklist item. The review button remains disabled while required profile information is incomplete. | Read the registration/renewal payment box and the current button label before continuing. | Click the displayed review/payment/renewal action. Complete checkout if a fee is due. | Return to the portal and check the pending review or registration-period result. | For a revision of an already settled period, correct the requested information and resubmit; the same period’s recorded payment is retained.
Expected result: The completed profile/renewal reaches the appropriate review state with its payment linked.

Scenario: Review vendor update requests
Actions / suggested test: Approve a bank/document change, reject another and check both vendor-visible statuses. Repeating a decision should not apply a second change.
Expected result: Profile changes have an identifiable reviewer and decision; pending/locked sections are not silently overwritten.

Scenario: Review a vendor, set a grade and assign its code
Actions / suggested test: Open the vendor and inspect registration, documents, contacts, bank details, branches, credentials and specialties. | Use the allowed status/grade action to record the review outcome. | For a fully registered vendor, open Edit and enter the optional Vendor Code text field. | Save and check the code on the vendor details. A second CR has its own vendor record/code.
Expected result: The reviewed vendor has the intended status, grade and company-specific code.

Scenario: Block, unblock or remove vendor access
Actions / suggested test: Block a designated test CR and verify its restrictions; unblock it and confirm the expected restored state.
Expected result: Access follows the company’s approved/blocked status and the saved reason.

Scenario: Check vendor payments and accounting records
Actions / suggested test: Search by the vendor/CR, transaction reference or available status/date filters. | Open the transaction details and read who paid, the payment purpose, amount, currency, status and bank references. | Compare the application transaction reference with the bank’s tracking/reference information. | Use the available recheck/export actions when appropriate. Review a charged-but-pending payment before asking the applicant to retry.
Expected result: Accounting can cross-reference registration, renewal and other vendor fee transactions.

Scenario: Understand the two starting routes
Actions / suggested test: Use the Department Request route when a department initiates the requirement: Requester → Department Manager → Finance → Committee request approval → Procurement tender creation. | Use New Tender in Procurement Inbox when procurement starts a tender directly. | Both routes still require the tender’s Procurement Manager approval before publication. | Read Request Source, Tender Status, Manager Approval and Workflow Stage separately in the inbox/register.
Expected result: The team knows which approvals belong to the request and which belong to the tender.

Scenario: Create a department tender request
Actions / suggested test: Save a draft, confirm it is not in the manager’s actionable queue, then Submit and confirm the handover.
Expected result: The request becomes Submitted and is available to its assigned Department Manager.

Scenario: Approve or reject the department request
Actions / suggested test: Open the submitted request and review the requirement, budget, teams and suggested vendors. | Approve if it is ready. Use Reject with a clear comment if it needs correction. | Confirm the decision. An approved request becomes Manager approved for Finance verification. | For rejection, the requester should read the reason, edit the request and submit it again.
Expected result: Only a submitted request is decided by its authorised Department Manager.

Scenario: Verify the request in Finance
Actions / suggested test: Open the Department Manager approved request. | Review its budget, requirement and approval history. | Use the Finance verification/approve action to continue, or Reject with a reason. | Check that an approved request becomes Finance verified and reaches Committee request review.
Expected result: Finance records a verification decision before committee request approval.

Scenario: Approve the request in Committee
Actions / suggested test: Open the Finance verified request. | Review the requirement, proposed teams/vendors and previous approvals. | Approve it, or reject it with a reason for correction. | Check that approved requests become Committee approved and are available to procurement for tender preparation.
Expected result: The approved department request can be converted into a procurement tender.

Scenario: Start the tender from a request or directly
Actions / suggested test: For a direct tender, click New Tender. | For an approved department request, use its available create/convert tender action; check the Linked request reference on the tender form. | Complete all six setup steps: Tender Details, Milestones, Team Assignment, Target Vendors, Documents, Preview. | Use Next/Previous or the step tabs to review the entire form before saving.
Expected result: A procurement draft contains the correct source and complete tender setup.

Scenario: Step 1 — tender details, method and fees
Actions / suggested test: Enter a unique Reference and a clear Title. Select Company and Department. | Choose Open for the open invitation route or Closed for a targeted vendor audience. | Choose the displayed Evaluation Method. Set Technical Weight and Commercial Weight; together they must equal 100%. | Enter Tender Fees in OMR. Zero means no tender fee; a positive amount creates the vendor fee requirement. | Write a clear Brief Description. Leave Submit for Procurement Manager Approval selected when ready for review.
Expected result: The tender’s identity, audience type, evaluation weighting and fee are explicit.

Scenario: Step 2 — set all tender dates
Actions / suggested test: Try opening before closing, equal opening/closing time, a Friday milestone and weights not totalling 100. Confirm invalid values are refused.
Expected result: The schedule is valid and defines when each user action is available.

Scenario: Step 3 — assign evaluators and opening members
Actions / suggested test: Choose the same person for two opening roles and check the form refuses it; verify all three assigned accounts see the correct tender.
Expected result: Each stage reaches its assigned users and three different roles can unlock bids.

Scenario: Step 4 — choose a flexible closed-tender audience
Actions / suggested test: Use one vendor matching all filters, one matching only some, one named extra and one unrelated vendor; confirm their visibility independently.
Expected result: Only the intended eligible CRs can see the closed tender when published.

Scenario: Step 5 — required proposals and item pricing
Actions / suggested test: Submit a bid with a missing required section and confirm it is refused. Check item quantities and computed line totals.
Expected result: Bidders know which files and priced items are required.

Scenario: Upload tender documents and control download access
Actions / suggested test: Click Add Document File and select the specification or other tender attachment. | Enter its title/type in the upload preview fields. | Set Download Access / time-limited access and expiry hours if the document should have limited download availability. | Review the uploaded file list and existing documents before saving. | For a published tender, submit the change for manager approval; pending new attachments are not vendor-visible until approved.
Expected result: Tender documents are saved with the intended title, type and visibility rules.

Scenario: Step 6 — preview and submit for manager approval
Actions / suggested test: Save without approval submission; then submit and verify the separate manager account receives it.
Expected result: A submitted tender remains unpublished while Manager Approval is Pending.

Scenario: Procurement Manager — approve, return or reject
Actions / suggested test: Run one approval and one return/revise/resubmit path using separate users.
Expected result: Approval authorises the next step; a revision sends the tender back to procurement with the comment.

Scenario: Publish an approved tender
Actions / suggested test: Try publication while manager approval is pending and confirm it is refused. Check a future release is not prematurely open.
Expected result: Eligible vendors can view the published tender during its permitted period.

Scenario: Change or extend tender dates after publication
Actions / suggested test: Propose an extension and compare vendor dates before and after manager approval. Try an invalid sequence and confirm it is rejected.
Expected result: Approved date changes become effective with a recorded old/new schedule.

Scenario: Vendor — find a tender, pay its fee and request participation
Actions / suggested test: Check the selected CR, tender title/reference and schedule. | Review Overview, Tender Details and available Tender Documents. | If a tender fee is required, use Pay Tender Fee before the purchase deadline and complete the approved bank checkout. | If Request procurement approval is shown, submit that request and wait for procurement’s decision. | When the fee/participation requirements are satisfied and bidding is open, the Bid Submission form becomes available.
Expected result: Only an eligible approved vendor can move to bid submission under the tender’s requirements.

Scenario: Procurement — approve vendor participation
Actions / suggested test: Approve one vendor and reject another; confirm neither decision changes unrelated vendors or another CR.
Expected result: Participation decisions apply only to the reviewed vendor/tender.

Scenario: Vendor — submit or update the full bid
Actions / suggested test: Try missing technical/commercial files, a valid full submission and an update before closing. Confirm no update is accepted after closing.
Expected result: The bid is submitted for the correct CR with its amount, item prices and required documents.

Scenario: Vendor — send a question to procurement
Actions / suggested test: Send General, Technical and Commercial questions with attachments. Confirm internal evaluator messages are not visible before procurement shares a reply.
Expected result: The question goes through procurement, including questions intended for the technical or commercial team.

Scenario: Procurement — reply, forward or publish to all vendors
Actions / suggested test: Send one private reply and one public reply. Check another vendor sees only the public one; check commercial-only internal attachments remain unavailable to the technical team.
Expected result: The selected visibility controls who receives the message and attached files.

Scenario: Technical/commercial team — respond through procurement
Actions / suggested test: Open the tender’s team clarification inbox/thread or the relevant bid’s evaluation screen. | Read the question forwarded by procurement and open the permitted attachments. | Reply internally to procurement with the answer and any supporting files. | For a new evaluator question, use the message/request clarification form. Identify the vendor/bid when the question is specific. | Procurement decides whether to relay the answer privately, publish it to eligible vendors or ask the vendor for further information.
Expected result: Procurement remains between vendors and evaluator teams.

Scenario: Publish an announcement, circular or tender group update
Actions / suggested test: Choose the displayed Update Type, such as an announcement/circular. | Enter a clear Subject and Message describing the update. | Attach the relevant supporting file(s). | Publish the update and check it in the communications list and an eligible vendor’s tender page.
Expected result: The tender’s permitted vendor audience can read the published update and attachment.

Scenario: Check the tender is ready for Bid Opening
Actions / suggested test: Wait until bid submission has closed and the scheduled opening time has arrived. | Confirm the tender is Closed and its Workflow Stage is Bid Opening. | Confirm Chairman, Secretary and Member are three different assigned users who can sign in. | Open the tender’s opening action in Bid Opening Inbox.
Expected result: The committee can begin the opening session for the correct closed tender.

Scenario: Generate the three role codes
Actions / suggested test: Check the reference/title and your assigned opening role. | Click Generate 3-Key Codes if no active session exists. | Note the displayed expiry time and coordinate the three people to confirm within it. | Each member opens their own session/account to retrieve only their assigned role code.
Expected result: A protected opening session holds separate Chairman, Secretary and Member codes.

Scenario: Each person confirms only their own role code
Actions / suggested test: Confirm only two roles and check bids stay locked; confirm the third and check unlock. Test an unassigned user and an expired code in designated test records.
Expected result: All three authorised confirmations are required before unlocking.

Scenario: Review the opened package and sign digitally
Actions / suggested test: Review every submitted vendor and the permitted technical, commercial and bank guarantee files. | Check the bid amounts, submitted information and package summary. | Enter Signature Name and draw your signature in the pad. | Select the confirmation checkbox and click Sign Bid Opening. | Each of the three people repeats this using their own account. Check Chairman, Secretary and Member all show Signed.
Expected result: The opening form records the three reviewers’ signatures and the completed opening state.

Role: Assigned committee / procurement with report access
Scenario: Print the official Bid Opening Record
Actions / suggested test: Print a tender with several bidders; check draft/non-submitted bids are not represented as submitted bids.
Expected result: The committee/procurement has a readable record in the approved template layout.

Scenario: Procurement — check proposals and start technical review
Actions / suggested test: Confirm all three signatures are complete and download/check the generated bid opening form. | Review the opened technical and commercial proposal package for completeness. | Select the generated-form confirmation checkbox and enter any Procurement Review Note. | Set the Technical Review Open Until date/time when requested and click Start Technical Review. | If an approved manual signed form is used as a fallback, upload it using the separate Manual Signed Bid Opening Form action and check acceptance first.
Expected result: The recorded procurement handover allows technical evaluators to begin.

Scenario: Technical evaluation — score, findings and decision
Actions / suggested test: Try a score above its criterion weight; check refusal. Verify technical users cannot open priced commercial files directly.
Expected result: The technical outcome and score are recorded; commercial prices stay outside the technical review screen.

Scenario: Commercial evaluation — review pricing and choose the outcome
Actions / suggested test: Check score limits, one selected bidder and one rejected bidder. Confirm an early commercial action before its stage is refused.
Expected result: The commercial outcome and weighted ranking support the final award decision.

Scenario: Review late evaluations before awarding
Actions / suggested test: Use a designated late evaluation and confirm award is refused until procurement records the required decision.
Expected result: Unreviewed late decisions do not silently become a final award basis.

Scenario: Finalise the tender award
Actions / suggested test: Attempt award too early and with pending late review. After a valid award, repeat the action and confirm no duplicate result letters are created.
Expected result: The winning bidder receives an award result; unsuccessful actual bidders receive regret results.

Scenario: Successful vendor — view the award letter
Actions / suggested test: Check another vendor’s login cannot retrieve the winner’s letter by changing the URL.
Expected result: The winning bidder can retain its own letter of award.

Scenario: Unsuccessful bidder — regret letter and email delivery
Actions / suggested test: Check one winner, one unsuccessful bidder and one invited non-bidder. Verify the correct letter/email recipient for each.
Expected result: Each unsuccessful actual bidder has its own regret letter; failed email delivery is visible and retryable.

Scenario: Use the Tender Register and audit tabs
Actions / suggested test: Search/filter tenders by reference and the available status/stage/company/date controls. | Use Overview for main facts and key dates; Tender Details for the item/terms schedule; Timeline for milestones. | Use Vendors for invitations, fee/participation and submitted bids; Evaluations for scores, findings and ranking. | Use Communications for messages/announcements and Documents & Audit for documents, extensions, workflow history and opening audit. | Use Edit Schedule and Bid Opening Form only when your role and the tender state allow them.
Expected result: The team can trace a tender from its source through approval, changes, opening and award.

Scenario: Cancel a tender through manager approval
Actions / suggested test: Review the tender and confirm cancellation is the intended business decision. | Use the cancellation action and confirm submission to the Procurement Manager. | The manager reviews the cancellation request and approves or returns/rejects it as appropriate. | Check the final tender status after the manager decision and the vendor-visible outcome.
Expected result: The cancellation is applied only through its required manager approval.

Scenario: Retender and formal workflow reopening
Actions / suggested test: For a retender, use Retender on the eligible source tender and open the new draft. | Review copied details, teams, audience and requirements. Enter a complete new valid schedule; do not assume the source deadlines remain suitable. | Submit the new draft for manager approval and publish it through the normal workflow. | For an exceptional stage reopening, select the intended stage, Stage Open Until and reason in Workflow Stage Control, then submit the request. | Obtain the manager decision and confirm the effective stage/time before telling users to act again.
Expected result: A retender is a new approved tender; an exceptional reopening is recorded and approved.

Scenario: Tender payment accounting
Actions / suggested test: Find the tender fee transaction by vendor/CR, tender/reference and the available filters. | Open details and confirm the payer, tender fee purpose, amount/currency, transaction status and bank references. | Compare the accounting outcome with the vendor’s fee state for that tender. | Export/recheck using the permitted actions when needed; investigate an existing charged/pending transaction before a new payment.
Expected result: Tender fee payments can be cross-referenced independently of vendor registration fees.

Scenario: Read statuses and respond to common problems
Actions / suggested test: If a button is missing, check the role, selected CR/company, assignment and current workflow stage. | If a vendor cannot participate, check registration, company approval/expiry/block status, invitation, tender fee, participation decision and date windows. | If a tender still says Draft, read Manager Approval. Pending approval is expected before publication; a saved-only draft needs submission. | If Bid Opening is unavailable, check closing/opening time, committee assignment, code expiry and whether another role still has to confirm/sign. | If an attachment does not open, report its reference/type and error; do not assume a successful upload proves it can be read. | If payment/SMS/email fails, record its displayed status/reference and report delivery separately from the saved application result.
Expected result: The report identifies the failed stage without guessing that the entire workflow was bypassed.

Role: Test coordinator and all assigned roles
Scenario: Run one full team acceptance test
Actions / suggested test: Register one paid vendor, one waived vendor and a separate waiver applicant asked to pay. Complete the correct documents and check the limited/full access boundaries. | Complete the profiles, add contacts, review updates and check email/CR/multi-CR sign-in with the required OTP policy. | Create one direct tender and one department request-route tender. Return one for revision, then approve and publish. | Check closed-tender filters and extra invitees; pay any authorised test tender fee and approve participation where required. | Exchange private, public, technical and commercial clarifications with attachments. Submit at least two full bids and check deadline restrictions. | Complete three different committee confirmations/signatures, print the opening record, then hand over to technical/commercial evaluation. | Review any late decisions, award one bidder and verify award/regret letters plus actual delivery statuses. | Record Passed, Failed, Blocked or Not tested for every checklist row. Send the completed checklist and issue screenshots to the coordinator.
Expected result: The team has an auditable full workflow result and a precise list of problems to report.

Scenario: What to include when reporting an issue
Actions / suggested test: Record the affected module, page name, tender/vendor/CR reference, user role and the date/time. | List the exact actions in order and what you expected. | Copy the visible error text and describe what actually happened. Include a screenshot showing the affected control/state. | For payment or delivery issues, include the application transaction/message reference and status. Do not include passwords, OTP codes or full card details. | Mark the relevant checklist row Failed or Blocked. Keep the original test record available for investigation.
Expected result: The support team can reproduce and locate the problem quickly.
